champion: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Tongue
ordered_diagnoses: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Tongue

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive bulbar and neck symptoms with weight loss
salient_findings: Constant pain at right occipital and cervical paraspinal areas
key_facts: Three-year history of worsening dysarthria and dysphagia
Choking episodes provoked when lying supine
One-year history of constant pain at right occipital and cervical paraspinal areas
20-pound weight loss
Right tongue deviation and atrophy
Limited tongue movements and difficulty with tongue protrusion
Lingual and palatal dysarthria
Normal laboratory tests including Acetylcholine receptor antibodies, TSH, B12, ANA, ESR, and CK
Active denervation changes on EMG
Infiltrative process at the base and root of the tongue on MRI
Enhancing, infiltrative, and partially necrotic mass on Maxillofacial CT
Focal, non-keratinizing invasive squamous cell carcinoma on biopsy

shortlist: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Tongue

shortlist.label: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Tongue
shortlist.why_kept: Biopsy results showed focal, non-keratinizing invasive squamous cell carcinoma, and imaging studies revealed an infiltrative process at the base and root of the tongue

shortlist.label: Hypoglossal Nerve Schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Right tongue deviation and atrophy, limited tongue movements, and difficulty with tongue protrusion could be related to a hypoglossal nerve schwannoma

shortlist.label: Oropharyngeal Cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Symptoms of dysarthria, dysphagia, and weight loss, along with imaging findings of an infiltrative process in the mouth floor, are consistent with oropharyngeal cancer

shortlist.label: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Infiltrative process at the base and root of the tongue and lymphatic tissue fullness on flexible laryngoscopy could be related to nasopharyngeal carcinoma

shortlist.label: Lingual Thyroid
shortlist.why_kept: Base of tongue fullness and prominent lymphatic tissue on flexible laryngoscopy could be related to a lingual thyroid, although less likely given the biopsy results

s4.champion: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Tongue

raw.champion: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Tongue
raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of worsening dysarthria and dysphagia, right tongue deviation and atrophy, and limited tongue movements are consistent with a tumor at the base of the tongue. The biopsy results showing focal, non-keratinizing invasive squamous cell carcinoma and the imaging studies demonstrating an infiltrative process at the base and root of the tongue support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Hypoglossal Nerve Schwannoma
rejected.why: The presence of an infiltrative mass and biopsy-proven squamous cell carcinoma makes this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Oropharyngeal Cancer
rejected.why: While this is a possible diagnosis, the specific location and biopsy results point more specifically to a squamous cell carcinoma of the tongue

rejected.label: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
rejected.why: The tumor's location at the base and root of the tongue, rather than the nasopharynx, makes this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Lingual Thyroid
rejected.why: The biopsy results and imaging studies do not support the presence of a thyroid tissue in the tongue
